title: A functor with a quasi-inverse induces bijections on Hom sets
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories [def-nagata-category], with objects and morphisms in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be functors, and suppose there are natural isomorphisms $GF\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $FG\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$. A functor preserves identities and composition, and naturality of an isomorphism means its components commute with every morphism. No triangle identities are assumed for these specified natural isomorphisms. For every $A,A\prime\in\mathcal A$, the function $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(A,A\prime)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(FA,FA\prime)$ sending $f$ to $F(f)$ is bijective.
